<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title/>
                    <jats:p>Hyperlipidemia, characterized by elevated blood lipid levels, represents a major global health
concern due to its strong association with cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and metabolic syndrome. While
current therapies - such as statins, fibrates, bile acid sequestrants, and PCSK9 inhibitors - are effective in
controlling hyperlipidemia, they are often associated with adverse effects, potential drug resistance, and
suboptimal efficacy in certain patient populations. All of the above underscore the urgent need for safer and
more effective therapeutic alternatives. Among the major molecular targets involved in the regulation of lipid
metabolism are HMG-CoA reductase, PCSK9, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs), cholesteryl
ester transfer protein (CETP), and nuclear receptors, including the liver X receptor (LXR) and farnesoid
X receptor (FXR), which are also targets for future antihyperlipidemic drug development. Recent advancements
in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have significantly transformed and accelerated
drug discovery by enabling the processing of vast amounts of genomic, proteomic, and chemical data.
Furthermore, ML tools such as quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) modelling, deep learning,
random forest, and support vector machines (SVM) have proven predictive and effective in identifying novel
lipid metabolism modulators, thereby enhancing the efficacy and accuracy of virtual screening. Meanwhile,
molecular docking has become an integral part of structure-based drug design (SBDD), and software such as
AutoDock, Glide, and GOLD have proven effective in generating accurate ligand–target docking models.
Molecular docking, together with ML-based approaches, enables the identification of potent and selective
drug candidates. Overall, the combination of ML and molecular docking offers an efficient and accurate
platform for antihyperlipidemic drug discovery, helping to overcome the limitations of currently available
therapeutic strategies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Machine Learning in Hyperlipidaemia Research: Screening and Experimental Insights into Lipid Metabolism Modulators

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The demand for inventive approaches to drug discovery has increased
due to the rising costs, time, and failure rates in pharmaceutical research. Large Language Models
(LLMs), with their sophisticated natural language processing and generative capabilities,
have become potent instruments that have the potential to revolutionize biomedical research.
The function of LLMs in different phases of drug development is methodically examined in this
article.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The PRISMA 2020 principles were adhered to in this systematic study. A thorough
search for research published between 2018 and 2025 was done using PubMed, Scopus, Web of
Science, and Google Scholar. The search terms "large language model," "transformer," "drug
discovery," and important sub-domains (such as "de-novo design" and "ADMET") were
merged, and two reviewers independently screened the results. Predetermined inclusion and exclusion
criteria were used to filter studies for relevance. 98 studies out of the 1,285 records that
were initially retrieved met the requirements for the final qualitative synthesis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>98 studies that demonstrated the use of LLMs in various drug discovery domains were
found during the review. These covered molecular generation, genomics, protein-ligand modeling,
ADME/T and toxicity profiling, drug-target interaction and DTI prediction, and biomedical
text mining. 42 different LLM-based tools were mapped, including BioBERT, SciSpacy, Drug-
LLM, DNA-BERT, GPT-4, and ChatGPT. Predictive accuracy, hypothesis creation, target prioritization,
and multi-modal data integration all showed notable gains with these techniques.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>By providing scalable, precise, and effective solutions for data-driven drug discovery,
LLMs are revolutionizing the pharmaceutical industry. They allow for the creation of hypotheses
and individualized insights across multi-modal biological data, and they perform better
than conventional approaches in a number of subdomains. Improvements in performance were
task-dependent; the most consistent gains occurred for biomedical text mining, disease-genedrug
relationship mapping and drug-target interaction prediction tasks. Yet most evidence for
clinical applications is still derived from retrospective studies and benchmark datasets, suggesting
a higher need for prospective validation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>There is revolutionary potential in incorporating LLMs into drug discovery processes.
Clinical translation and regulatory uptake will depend heavily on collaborative validation,
ethical deployment, and standardization as models become more multimodal and interpretable.
Before normal use, extensive prospective benchmarking and head-to-head comparisons
with established chemoinformatics pipelines are necessary.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title:
Harnessing the Power of Large Language Models for Drug Discovery: A
Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Directions

<jats:p>Digital contracting has made contractual assent almost frictionless. Consumers routinely enter into contractual relationships by clicking 'I Agree' to standard-form terms that may contain extensive provisions concerning liability, dispute resolution, automatic renewal, intellectual property, indemnification and termination. Contract law, however, generally does not require proof that a contracting party actually read or understood every contractual provision before becoming bound. This creates a persistent tension between the formal manifestation of assent and the informational circumstances in which that assent is obtained.

This article examines that tension through the concept of the 'assent-comprehension gap', the distance between the legal significance attributed to an affirmative act of acceptance and the extent to which the contracting party could reasonably appreciate the consequences of that act. It argues that the solution lies neither in requiring actual comprehension nor in treating a single click as equally meaningful for every term in a standard-form agreement. Instead, it proposes a graduated model of meaningful assent, under which the procedural conditions surrounding acceptance become increasingly important as the materiality and consequences of a term increase.

The article situates this proposal within Indian contract law and consumer protection law, considering the recognition of electronic contracting under the Information Technology Act, 2000. It engages with Robert A. Hillman's analysis of Internet standard-form contracts in India and the broader 'no-reading problem' literature, and draws on comparative clickwrap and browsewrap jurisprudence to illustrate how courts have approached the relationship between notice and affirmative assent.

Building on this analysis, the article develops a five-factor framework based on materiality, prominence, complexity, consequence and transactional context, and concludes that this framework can preserve contractual certainty while preventing the act of clicking 'I Agree' from becoming detached from the significance of the obligations it is taken to create.</jats:p>
title: The Assent-Comprehension Gap: Rethinking Meaningful Assent in Digital Standard-Form Contracts

items.abstract: The challenge of predicting placement outcomes is a recurring one among engineering institutions because of the complex, non-linear interplay of various academic performance, technical proficiency, soft skills, and socio-economic aspects. Traditional machine learning models are often unable to capture these non-linear relationships, and their performance is limited to less than 85% accuracy. In comparison, hyperparameter tuning of deep learning models is still time-consuming and computationally expensive when done manually or by a grid search. In this work, a novel three-stage hybrid optimization framework combining Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Bayesian Optimization (BayOpt) is proposed to optimize, independently, the hyperparameters of an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) in the placement prediction task. This framework is for a general global search using PSO, evolutionary refinement using GA, and high-accuracy fine-tuning using Bayesian Optimization, which is implemented using Optuna. Concurrently, Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) is employed to tackle the class imbalance problem and provide unbiased predictions. The proposed hybrid AI (PSO + GA+Bayesian + ANN) model was tested on a large-scale dataset of Indian engineering students with 5000 entries and 22 features across five categories, with a high test accuracy of 99.60%, which is much higher than the baseline models like XGBoost, Random Forest, Decision Trees, and Naïve Bayes, with precision, recall, and F1 > 0.95 for both classes. Through feature importance analysis, the most important features found to determine the placement were coding skill rating, CGPA, and completed projects. Beyond merely predicting "black boxes," post-hoc SHAP and LIME explainability techniques confirmed the global feature ranking, identified a saturation effect after approximately 8.0/10 features, and provided clear, student-level explanations of the results of each prediction. Overall, the framework provides an early warning system in early education and schools that is both reliable and interpretable and promotes designing the education curriculum in alignment with the needs of the industry and targeted interventions that enhance employability outcomes.
title: An Interpretable Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Student Placement Prediction Using PSO–GA–Bayesian Optimized ANN with SHAP–LIME Explainability

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction/Objective:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The progressive nature of dementia is represented by a reduction in two or more cognitive functions, including language, memory, executive and visuospatial functioning, personality, and behavior. Only symptoms can be alleviated by traditional medication therapies. A strategy that shows promise for focused and customized interventions is gene therapy, especially when combined with artificial intelligence (AI).This review investigates the integration of AI with gene delivery technologies to enhance the accuracy, effectiveness, and personalization of dementia therapies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>PRISMA guidelines were followed in conducting a systematic review. A literature search for English-language articles published between 2012 and 2026 was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Peer-reviewed original research, computational studies, or reviews; attention to AI in the context of gene delivery in dementia; and pertinence to biological mechanisms or therapeutic approaches were the inclusion criteria. Non-English papers, conference abstracts, letters, editorials, and research unrelated to gene delivery or dementia were among the exclusion criteria. The full texts, abstracts, and titles were vetted by two separate reviewers. Discussions or seeking advice from a third reviewer were used to settle disagreements.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI has proven to be very helpful in predicting therapeutic targets, optimizing gene vectors, and customizing dementia treatment plans. Using machine learning and deep learning approaches, it also makes gene-target prediction, nanocarrier optimization, and post-treatment monitoring easier. These methods improve vector design, find biomarkers, and decode complex genomic data. Precision gene delivery across the blood-brain barrier is now possible because to integration with (Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic repeat) CRISPR/Cas9, adeno-associated virus vectors, and lipid nanoparticles, which has increased transfection efficiency and decreased cytotoxicity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Precision medicine is becoming possible because of AI frameworks that integrate neuroimaging, multi-omics data, and patient-specific genomic profiles. Notwithstanding the potential, there are still issues including data security, ethical dilemmas, translational barriers, and legal limitations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Gene Delivery Systems in Dementia: A Comprehensive Review of Mechanisms, Tools, and Therapeutic Strategies

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>introduction:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to synthesize, characterize, and evaluate the toxicity of luteolin- and fisetin-loaded zinc oxide nanoparticles (LF-ZnONPs) as a potential therapeutic strategy for neurodegenerative diseases, particularly Parkinson’s disease (PD).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>materials and methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>LF-ZnONPs were chemically synthesised and characterised using UV–visible spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). Antioxidant activity was assessed through the DPPH radical scavenging assay. Drug loading, encapsulation efficiency, and in vitro release were analysed. Acute and subacute toxicity studies were performed in Wistar rats following OECD guidelines to establish the safety profile.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>LF-ZnONPs were predominantly spherical, with particle sizes ranging from 50 to 100 nm, and exhibited high crystallinity and stability. FTIR confirmed flavonoid–ZnO interactions, while TGA verified successful drug incorporation. The nanoparticles demonstrated strong antioxidant activity, with an encapsulation efficiency of 90.36% and sustained release of 57.88% within 40 minutes. Acute toxicity testing indicated a median lethal dose (LD₅₀) of ~1667 mg/kg, reflecting low acute toxicity. Subacute studies revealed mild, dose-dependent effects at higher concentrations (500–750 mg/kg), while biochemical and histopathological evaluations confirmed safety at lower doses.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>discussion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results suggest that LF-ZnONPs provide synergistic antioxidant and neuroprotective benefits while maintaining a favourable safety margin. Further mechanistic and pharmacological investigations in PD models are warranted to validate their translational potential.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>LF-ZnONPs effectively integrate the neuroprotective properties of luteolin and fisetin with the favourable characteristics of ZnO nanocarriers. These findings highlight their potential as a safe and efficient nanomedicine-based strategy for managing PD and related neurodegenerative disorders.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Molecular Engineering of Metallic Nanoparticle Using Natural Flavonoids: From Synthesis to Biological Evaluation

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Cancer is a major global health challenge, with p53 mutations occurring in
over 50% of human cancers and contributing to impaired DNA repair and apoptosis. In more recent
work, phytochemicals in herbs such as curcumin, resveratrol, genistein, berberine, and withaferin A
were found to enhance p53 activity or rescue it in cancer treatment by amplifying the apoptotic effects
or tumor-suppressive functions of p53-activated pathways. This review evaluates the effects of
curcumin, resveratrol, genistein, berberine, withaferin A, apigenin, betulinic acid, and piperlongumine
on the p53 tumor suppressor pathway in cancer, focusing on their ability to restore p53 activity
and increase fast apoptosis in cancer cells.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A comprehensive literature search from 2014 to 2026 was conducted using PubMed, ScienceDirect,
and Google Scholar with predefined keywords related to p53, phytochemicals, and cancer.
Relevant studies were selected using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Result:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The reviewed evidence indicates that phytochemicals, including curcumin, resveratrol, berberine,
genistein, and withaferin A, enhance p53 signaling, promote apoptosis, and induce G1/S cellcycle
arrest, thereby suppressing tumor growth, metastasis, and treatment resistance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Phytochemicals exert multitarget effects on the p53 pathway but face clinical limitations
due to poor bioavailability, pharmacokinetic variability, and tumor heterogeneity. Further clinical
studies and advanced drug-delivery systems are needed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The use of phytotherapeutic agents targeting the p53 pathway offers a promising, lowtoxicity
approach for cancer treatment. They impede malignancy and restore cellular regulation by
modulating p53 signaling. Further clinical research, improved bioavailability, and incorporation into
current pharmaceuticals are essential for validating phytotherapy as a viable method for cancer treatment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title:
Phytochemical Modulation of the p53 Tumor Suppressor Pathway: Mechanistic Insights, Translational Evidence, and Therapeutic Perspectives
in Cancer

items.abstract: In the current investigation, a Williamson hybrid nanofluid flows through a permeable stretched cylinder in a steady-state, laminar, incompressible mode. Non-linear ODEs are derived from the framed equations for energy, momentum, and mass by applying appropriate similarity variables. The BVP5c solution in MATLAB effectively applies the RK method to the boundary value problem. The novelty of this research is the comprehensive analysis of Williamson HNF ( Ag–SiC/H 2 O ) flow over a permeable stretching cylinder under the simultaneous influence of MHD, porosity, Williamson parameter, radiation, heat source/sink, viscous dissipation, and chemical reaction with activation energy. It addresses the lack of integrated multi-physics modelling for shear-thinning hybrid nanofluids by capturing the coupled effects of non-Newtonian behaviour within a unified computational framework. Furthermore, for nanofluid and hybrid nanofluid, the wall shear factor rate of heat and solute transmission is computed. Additionally, we verified the data by comparing them with previously published publications and found strong correspondence, which confirms the authenticity of the present investigation. For the relevant parameters, a thorough change in temperature, concentration, and velocity is investigated. Considering aligned angle, porosity, and MHD, a decrease in velocity is noted. We observe an improved HNF temperature for activation energy, MHD, radiation, and Eckert number. Moreover, when temperature, Schmidt number, and chemical reaction increase, the concentration distribution declines. The findings are relevant to advanced thermal systems, including cooling of electronic devices, nuclear reactors, chemical reactors, energy storage systems, biomedical heat transfer, and industrial processes involving magnetically controlled and radiative fluid flows.
title: Computational Assessment of Magneto-Radiative and Activation Energy Influences on Heat and Mass Transmission in Williamson Hybrid Nanofluid Ag- SiC/Water Flow over a Permeable Stretching Cylinder

items.abstract: A 2-port graphene-silicon-built THz antenna is planned and examined in this communication. Aperture feeding and air cavities in silicon dielectric are used to achieve wideband features i.e. 2.35-3.8 THz. Three unique features of designed antenna are: (i) circular metallic rings added with printed line to notched the frequency band, i.e., 2.75-3.15 THz; (ii) Deep neural network (DNN) and Random Forest (RF) are applied to guess |S11| parameter of the designed radiator; and (iii) presence of DGS reduces the coupling below -25 dB. Graphene layering assists in providing frequency tunability qualities to the planned antenna. CST and HFSS EM software confirm the final outcome that the planned antenna works in between 2.2-2.65 THz and 3.3-3.7 THz. A Stable radiation feature and good multi-port parameters confirm its applicability for mobile communication in the THz regime.

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Dopaminergic neuronal loss, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative
stress, and neurotransmitter imbalance are the hallmarks of Parkinson's Disease (PD), a progressive
neurodegenerative disorder. Despite their established antioxidant and neuroprotective qualities,
the mechanistic significance of Juglans regia L. and Cardiospermum halicacabum L. in
Parkinson's disease remains unclear, especially in the context of extract-based treatment approaches.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Drug-likeness and ADMET properties were evaluated with SwissADME and ADMETlab
3.0, respectively. SwissTargetPrediction was used to predict potential targets of selected
phytoconstituents, whereas gene sets associated with Parkinson's disease were mined from Dis-
GeNET and GeneCards. Venn analysis was performed to identify overlapping targets for drugs,
followed by Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) network construction using STRING and topological
analysis in Cytoscape. Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG pathway enrichment analysis were
performed using DAVID 2021, then a Bioactive Compound-Target-Pathway (BA-TAR-PATH)
network was constructed. Molecular docking based on AutoDock Vina was used to predict
the binding affinity between the protein and ligand for the top 10 hits; then, molecular
dynamics simulation using GROMACS was applied to assess the stability of the protein-ligand
complexes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Result:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Phytochemical characterization by HPTLC, FTIR, HPLC, and ESI-MS supported the
presence of flavonoids, phenolic compounds, tannins, and lipid-associated constituents in the
combined extract. Target prediction yielded 355 related compounds and 30 PD-associated genes,
identifying five overlapping targets (ACHE, DRD2, MAOB, COMT, and SLC6A3). Molecular
docking revealed favourable binding interactions, particularly quercetin-ACHE (-11.4 kcal/mol),
while molecular dynamics simulations supported the stability of selected protein-ligand complexes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Network analysis highlighted MAOB, COMT, and SLC6A3 as key hub genes. GO
and KEGG analyses revealed significant enrichment of dopaminergic synapse, neuroactive ligand–
receptor signalling, and Parkinson disease pathways. Molecular docking demonstrated stable
binding interactions, notably quercetin-ACHE (-11.4 kcal/mol), supporting the therapeutic
relevance of flavonoids.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Based on the above findings, we propose that both J. regia kernel and C. halicacabum
seed extracts may contain phytoconstituents that interact with various PD-related targets
and pathways linked to dopaminergic neurotransmission and oxidative stress. This extractanchored
network pharmacology approach presents a mechanism-related framework to facilitate
follow-up experiments targeting specific bioactive constituents and molecular targets. At the
same time, the results come exclusively from computational analyses and should be treated as
hypothesis-generating. In vitro, in vivo, and pharmacokinetic studies need to be performed to
validate the biological activity and therapeutic relevance experimentally.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title:
Unravelling Anti-parkinson’s Potential of Combined Extracts of Juglans
regia L. and Cardiospermum halicacabum L. through an in silico Approach

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Herbal medicines contain complex phytochemicals that offer therapeutic potential, but their long-term adverse effects remain challenging to determine. Traditional herbal medicine preparation methods are often labor-intensive, non-standardized, and face difficulties in identifying active ingredients. By improving medication development, optimization, and discovery procedures, Artificial Intelligence (AI) provides innovative ways to get beyond these restrictions. This systematic review aims to evaluate the role of AI-based software such as LEAFSNAP, Deep-Chem, PlantNet, Autodock, MestReNova, XCMS, ADMETlab, SynergyFinder, KEGG, TCMID, and Reactome in enhancing phytomedicine research by streamlining plant identification, bioactive com-pound discovery, molecular modeling, and pharmacokinetic profiling, thereby advancing drug dis-covery and development processes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA guidelines) to explore the integration of AI-based tools in phytomedicine research and drug discovery. Literature searches were performed in Scopus, PubMed, and Google Scholar databases, focusing on studies published between January 2015 and January 2025. Only English-language articles focusing on AI-based software for drug discovery from plant-derived compounds were reviewed. Studies discussing synthetic drug development were ex-cluded; this, along with non-English language, acted as a literature review limitation. Two reviewers independently screened the titles, abstracts, and full texts of the retrieved articles. Any discrepancies in the screening, study selection, and data extraction processes were resolved through discussion and consensus.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Through the effective identification of bioactive chemicals and the simplification of intricate studies, the combination of artificial intelligence and computer tools has completely transformed the process of discovering and developing herbal drugs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Artificial intelligence tools like ADMETlab for pharmacokinetics and toxicity assess-ments, DeepChem for molecular activity modelling, and AlphaFold for protein structure prediction have greatly improved the search for new herbal drugs. While AutoDock improves molecular docking simulations by automating ligand-receptor binding predictions for bioactive chemicals, LeafSnap and PlantNet make plant identification simpler. Drug development workflows are improved by databases such as KEGG and TCMID, which combine pathway analysis with conventional medical knowledge.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Research on phytomedicine may reach its full potential if AI techniques are improved and traditional knowledge and contemporary technology are better integrated.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Artificial Intelligence-powered Advances in Phytomedicine: A Systematic Review on Plant-based Drug Discovery Software

items.abstract: <jats:p>Cavitation-induced surface degradation severely limits the service life of stainless-steel components employed in hydraulic and fluid-handling systems because repeated bubble collapse generates localised shock waves and microjets capable of initiating plastic deformation, cracking, and progressive material removal. Therefore, developing a dense and mechanically robust surface layer capable of resisting such repeated impact loading is essential for improving the durability of these components. In the present study, WC + 50%NiCrB composite claddings were developed on SS410 stainless steel using laser cladding and their water-jet cavitation erosion behaviour was investigated under varying impingement conditions. The developed cladding exhibited a dense microstructure with retained spherical WC particles uniformly embedded within the NiCrB matrix and an average thickness of 471 ± 2.39 μm. Elemental mapping confirmed the homogeneous distribution of W, C, Ni, Cr, Fe, and B throughout the cladded region. Localised hardness measurements revealed average hardness values of 582 ± 31 HV for the NiCrB matrix and 2283 ± 76 HV for the WC particles. Water-jet cavitation erosion tests were performed by varying jet velocity (25–35 m/s), impact angle (30–90°), and nozzle-to-specimen distance (4–12 cm). The mass loss increased with increasing jet velocity and impact angle, whereas the maximum erosion was observed at an intermediate nozzle-to-specimen distance of 8 cm. Under all operating conditions, the WC + 50%NiCrB composite cladding exhibited lower material loss than the substrate. The harshest condition corresponded to a jet velocity of 35 m/s, an impact angle of 90°, and a nozzle-to-specimen distance of 8 cm.</jats:p>
title: Water jet cavitation erosion behaviour of WC reinforced NiCrB composite claddings under varying impingement conditions

However, traditional black-box AI models often reduce trust and transparency in cybersecurity decisions. This chapter explores human-centered Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for improving interpretable threat detection, anomaly analysis, risk prioritization, and analyst decision-making. It also presents an AIoT-based “Explainable Intelligent SOC Monitoring System for Smart Enterprise Networks” integrating IoT network sensors, edge devices, AI intrusion detection, SHAP and LIME explainability, federated learning, and adaptive alert prioritization. A real-time SOC dashboard provides attack explanations, threat scores, and response support. Human–AI collaboration, analyst feedback, fairness, bias mitigation, trust, accountability, and regulatory concerns are also discussed to support more transparent, reliable, and trustworthy cyber defense systems.</jats:p>

                    ) at the GGA‐PBE level, with corrected TB‐mBJ + SOC values of 6.00 and 4.69 eV, respectively. Optical property calculations reveal high absorption coefficients (~10
                    <jats:sup>6</jats:sup>
                     cm
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ) in the ultraviolet region, with optical onsets corresponding to the calculated bandgaps (3.82 and 3.29 eV at the PBE + SOC level, or 6.00 and 4.69 eV at the TB‐mBJ + SOC level). No significant visible‐light absorption is observed, consistent with the wide bandgap nature of these compounds. The thermoelectric figure of merit (ZT) reaches 0.70 for FrBaBr
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    and 0.66 for FrBaI
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    at 1200 K, assuming ideal crystal structures and within the limitations of the constant relaxation time approximation. All conclusions regarding application potential are theoretical and require experimental validation. Francium's radioactivity and extreme scarcity constrain the practical feasibility of these materials.

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Dendrimers are highly ordered nanoscale macromolecules characterized by well-defined architecture, monodispersity, and broad surface functionality. Their customizable physicochemical properties make them ideal drug-delivery vehicles for overcoming the constraints of traditional treatments.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A narrative literature synthesis was undertaken using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Recent research focusing on dendrimer production, structural properties, drug-loading processes, targeted techniques, therapeutic uses, and clinical translation was critically appraised.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Dendrimers demonstrated considerable benefits for regulated drug encapsulation, accurate surface functionalization, and targeted administration of a wide variety of therapeutic and diagnostic agents. Surface-engineered dendrimer systems consistently boosted bioavailability, decreased systemic toxicity, and promoted site-specific drug accumulation, therefore boosting therapeutic effectiveness. Their applications range beyond cancer, gene and nucleic acid delivery, infectious illnesses, neurological disorders, and theranostic platforms. Furthermore, some clinically evaluated dendrimer-based systems have exhibited remarkable translational potential, underscoring their possibility for future therapeutic applications.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Despite impressive improvements, numerous fundamental difficulties remain that limit the general clinical translation of dendrimer-based nanomedicines. These include generation-dependent cytotoxicity, poor biodegradability in some dendrimer designs, large-scale manufacturing and batch-to-batch repeatability challenges, as well as rigorous regulatory and quality control requirements. Addressing these restrictions via rational molecular design, scalable manufacturing methodologies, and standardized regulatory frameworks will be critical for effective clinical translation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Dendrimers are a highly adaptable and promising family of next-generation nanocarriers with great potential for precise drug delivery and improved therapeutic applications. Nevertheless, continued efforts toward developing safer and biodegradable dendrimer architectures, establishing cost-effective and scalable manufacturing processes, and generating robust preclinical and clinical evidence are imperative to facilitate their successful integration into routine clinical practice.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Recent Progress in Dendrimer-based Drug Delivery Systems: Therapeutic Strategies and Clinical Outlook

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In this study, the improved heat transfer and thermodynamic irreversibility analysis of magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) slip flow past an exponentially stretching sheet in a silver-based nanofluid in a porous medium are investigated. To extend the existing literature, the combined effects of thermal radiation, Brownian motion, thermophoresis, and viscous dissipation across Ag–blood, Ag–water, Ag–ethylene glycol, and Ag–kerosene nanofluids are considered. Analytical solutions are derived using the Homotopy perturbation method (HPM), while MATLAB bvp4c solver is used for numerical validation. After deriving the mathematical formulation and validating its accuracy, the impact of governing physical parameters on velocity, temperature, concentration, and entropy generation profiles is evaluated. The results establish various critical insights into fluid dynamics as well as thermodynamic behaviour. Enhancement in nanoparticle concentration and magnetic field strength considerably increases thermal boundary layer thickness in addition to total entropy generation, a systematic downward shift in local Nusselt number is perceived as magnetic parameter
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    increases from 0 to 5. In addition, the aggregating nanoparticle concentration and magnetic field strength considerably increased the thermal boundary layer thickness, in addition to the total entropy generation. Eventually, the study envisions the significant role of fluid selection and porous media resistance in optimizing thermal systems, proposing a viable pathway for minimizing thermal irreversibility in advanced engineering and physiological applications.
                  </jats:p>
title: A comparative analysis between different Ag based nanomaterials over an exponentially stretching sheet with entropy and velocity slip by using perturbation and numerical approaches

                  <jats:p>
                    Integrating renewable energy sources (RES) into power grids can benefit the environment and economy. The inclusion of conventional systems, creates problems due to the unpredictability and intermittency of RES. A load frequency controller (LFC) is essential for solving these challenges. The implementation of devices referred to as Mobile Electric Vehicle Energy Storage (MEVES) is being used in the regulation of grid frequency by storing surplus renewable energy generated at peak production times. This research investigates the issues of integrating RES into electric power networks. A hybrid ZOA-PS PI-(1 + DD) controller is put forward. The system’s performance is evaluated alongside controllers employing OOA-PS, IWO-PS, GWO-PS, AVOA-PS, and ABC-PS optimization methods. Evaluation with MEVES and RES integration demonstrates the efficacy of the controller. With regard to Δ

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the selective degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta, culminating in debilitating motor dysfunction. The consequent deficit in dopamine bioavailability, exacerbated by excessive Monoamine Oxidase-B (MAO-B)-mediated oxidative catabolism, underscores the continued search for pharmacologically active phytochemicals from validated medicinal plants. Our preceding computational investigation demonstrated that Apigenin, a flavonoid constituent of Solanum nigrum L., exhibits the highest MAO-B binding affinity (−9.8 to −10.0 kcal/mol) among 29 screened phytoconstituents, warranting experimental validation. Objective: The present study aimed to isolate and spectroscopically characterize Apigenin (designated compound GK-05) from Solanum nigrum L. and to evaluate its in vivo neuroprotective potential in a rotenone-induced Drosophila melanogaster model of Parkinson's disease. Methods: Dried aerial parts of S. nigrum were subjected to sequential solvent extraction, and the ethyl acetate fraction was purified by silica gel column chromatography. The isolated compound was characterized by ¹H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl₃), ¹³C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl₃), COSY, HMBC, HSQC, and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESIMS). For in vivo evaluation, wild-type Canton-S Drosophila melanogaster males were exposed to rotenone (500 µM) to induce PD-like phenotypes and co-treated with Apigenin (GK fraction, 20 and 40 ppm), with L-DOPA (0.5 mM) as positive control. Neurobehavioral assessment employed the negative geotaxis assay, and survival was monitored over seven days. Results: GK-05 was confirmed as Apigenin (4ʹ,5,7-trihydroxyflavone; C₁₅H₁₀O₅; MW 270.24 g/mol) by comprehensive spectral analysis. Flies co-treated with 20 ppm Apigenin (20GK+R) demonstrated statistically significant improvement in locomotor performance compared to the rotenone control group, approaching near-control climbing indices. L-DOPA co-treatment similarly restored locomotor function; however, the 40GK+R group did not exhibit significant locomotor recovery. Survival analysis revealed no statistically significant difference among any treatment group relative to the rotenone group. Conclusion: Apigenin isolated from Solanum nigrum L. confers dose-specific, functionally significant neuroprotection against rotenone-induced motor deficits in Drosophila melanogaster, corroborating in silico MAO-B inhibition data from our earlier study. These findings position Apigenin as a promising lead candidate for further mechanistic and translational investigations in Parkinson's disease therapy.</jats:p>
title: Isolation, Spectral Characterization, and In Vivo Neuroprotective Evaluation of Apigenin from Solanum nigrum L. in a RotenoneInduced Drosophila melanogaster Model of Parkinson's Disease

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Remote sensing satellite imagery has become an important tool in change
detection and is essential for monitoring the environment, urban development, and land use. Conventional
approaches often fail to reflect the subtle geospatial and temporal changes that comprise dynamic
landscapes. The availability of satellite and aerial imagery has revealed the need for sophisticated
algorithms. Recent deep learning developments have potential for satellite image analysis because
they can extract features and recognize patterns.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The proposed early fusion framework incorporates a UNet++ architecture with a Reg-
NetY_016 backbone, reinforced with SCSE attention mechanisms in the decoder block. By learning
hierarchical features, the proposed model effectively captures fine spatial details and subtle variations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Comprehensive testing on Szada/1 and Tiszadob/3, on standard splits used for comparison with
existing state-of-the-art methods, achieves F1-scores of 75.54% and 92.68%, respectively. The method also
outperforms with an average F1-score of 87.87% ± 4.30% (Szada) and 93.72% ± 1.55% (Tiszadob) under 5-
fold cross-validation on the full datasets across different data splits.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Ablation experiments and computational complexity analysis validate that both nested
skip connections and the SCSE attention module boost the detection performance with minimal
computational overhead. Cross-region experiments further confirm the proposed model’s transferability
across distinct datasets.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These results show that deep learning architectures coupled with specialized attention
mechanisms are viable approaches for robust performance on change detection tasks in bi-temporal
satellite images.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Enhancing Semantic Segmentation-based Change Detection in Bi-temporal Satellite Images

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Polylactic acid (PLA) composites reinforced with graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) offer potential for sustainable, high‐performance additive manufacturing. This study investigates the influence of graphene loading, layer height, infill density, and nozzle temperature on the mechanical behavior of fused deposition modeling (FDM)‐fabricated graphene/PLA composites. A Taguchi L27 orthogonal array was employed to design the experiments, and tensile strength, compressive strength, and Shore D hardness were evaluated experimentally. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was used to examine graphene distribution, matrix–reinforcement contact, interlayer continuity, void formation, and fracture characteristics. Increasing graphene content was associated with improved microstructural continuity and fewer visible interfacial defects. The composite containing 1.5 wt% graphene, printed at a layer height of 0.1 mm, 100% infill density, and a nozzle temperature of 220°C, exhibited the highest observed mechanical responses, with tensile strength of 67.42 MPa, compressive strength of 81.35 MPa, and Shore D hardness of 82.4. Artificial neural network (ANN), gene expression programming (GEP), and response surface methodology (RSM) models were developed and compared using the coefficient of determination (
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    ), root mean square error (RMSE), and mean absolute error (MAE). ANN demonstrated the best predictive performance, achieving
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    values of 0.982, 0.978, and 0.971 for tensile strength, compressive strength, and hardness, respectively. Confirmation experiments yielded prediction errors below 1% for all three responses using ANN. The integrated experimental and computational framework supports mechanical performance prediction and process‐parameter assessment for graphene‐reinforced PLA composites within the investigated experimental domain.
                  </jats:p>
title:
Intelligent Modeling of Mechanical Behavior in

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The rapid expansion of optical communication networks has increased the demand for intelligent monitoring, fault prediction, and adaptive network management techniques. Conventional optical network management approaches rely mainly on periodic measurements and predefined threshold-based decisions, which are unable to efficiently handle dynamic network conditions. This paper proposes an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven digital twin framework for real-time performance monitoring and fault prediction in optical communication networks. The proposed digital twin creates a virtual representation of the physical optical network by continuously collecting important network parameters, including received optical power, optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR), bit error rate (BER), quality factor (Q-factor), and transmission distance. An artificial neural network (ANN)-based prediction model is integrated with the digital twin to identify abnormal network conditions and predict possible performance degradation. The proposed approach is evaluated under different optical transmission scenarios by varying fiber length, noise level, and signal power. Simulation results demonstrate that the AI-enabled digital twin provides accurate prediction of optical link conditions and improves network monitoring capability compared with conventional machine learning approaches. The proposed framework achieves high prediction accuracy with low computational complexity, making it suitable for future intelligent optical communication networks. The proposed method achieves an accuracy of 98.9 %, demonstrating its effectiveness in monitoring network performance and accurately predicting faults in optical communication networks.</jats:p>
title: AI-driven digital twin for performance monitoring and fault prediction in optical communication networks

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Here, we develop and validate a machine‐learning (ML) framework for rapid screening and prediction of hydrogen‐storage performance in perovskite hydrides (ABH
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    ), using 17 physicochemical descriptors derived from 1000 DFT‐calculated compounds. Efficient solid‐state hydrogen storage is critical for sustainable energy, but exhaustive DFT screening of the thousands of possible perovskite‐hydride (ABH
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    ) compositions is computationally prohibitive. Here a ML framework was developed and validated on 1000 DFT‐derived ABH
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    compounds described by 17 physicochemical descriptors, benchmarking Random Forest, XGBoost, SVR, Decision Tree, Linear Regression, and a stacking ensemble across five target properties. On a genuinely held‐out 200‐compound test set, the optimized stacking ensemble reached
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                     = 0.994 for hydrogen‐storage capacity and F1 = ROC‐AUC = 1.000 for stability and magnetic‐ordering classification; formation energy (
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                     = 0.755) and bulk modulus (
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                     = 0.749) proved harder to predict, reflecting genuine descriptor‐property limits rather than model failure. A SISSO‐style symbolic‐regression search distilled the ensemble into a transparent two‐term formula (summed A‐/B‐site atomic mass and its product;
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                     = 0.838, test), recovering the model's learned physics with no black‐box component. SHAP, LIME, permutation importance, and UMAP consistently identify A‐/B‐site atomic mass as the dominant driver of storage capacity, yielding a design threshold (M
                    <jats:sub>a</jats:sub>
                     + Mᵇ ≤ 202.5 amu) satisfied by all 15 top‐ranked candidates (KScH
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    , NaCoH
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    , CaNiH
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    , among others). Benchmarked against AB5 (LaNi
                    <jats:sub>5</jats:sub>
                    , 1.2–1.5 wt%) and AB2 (TiMn
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    , 1.8–2.2 wt%) intermetallic hydrides, the explored ABH
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    space reaches up to 8.19 wt%. Inference across all 1000 compounds completes in under 100 ms after an 18‐s training step, versus hours‐to‐weeks per DFT calculation. A statistically significant but weak, mass‐confounded relationship between magnetic ordering and storage capacity is reported, correcting an earlier overstated trade‐off.
                  </jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>High-speed visible-light communication (VLC) using gallium-nitride micro–light-emitting diodes (micro-LEDs) is sensitive to thermal variations that can degrade predistortion accuracy and link performance. This numerical study proposes and evaluates thermally robust adaptive compensation and entropy loading (TRACEL), a self-calibrating physical-layer method for direct-current–biased optical orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (DCO-OFDM). Here, self-calibration means that the coefficients of the inverse are estimated online; the junction temperature is assumed to be known, and no hardware is calibrated. TRACEL employs complementary odd-symmetric probes that preserve average optical current, event-triggered recursive least squares to update a nine-term memory-polynomial inverse, subcarrier-level covariance projection for distortion reservation, and capped water filling with Maxwell–Boltzmann entropy selection under a fourth-moment peak-risk constraint. A 256-point DCO-OFDM link with 96 data subcarriers and 4-GS/s sampling is evaluated using a temperature-dependent micro-LED behavioral model whose bandwidth decreases from 1.62 to 1.21 GHz over 25–85 °C. Under a 25–85–25 °C thermal cycle, TRACEL achieves 6.902 Gbit/s net achievable information rate, 17.59 % error-vector magnitude (EVM), and 0.392 service-outage probability, compared with 6.507 Gbit/s, 21.00 %, and 0.522 for static joint loading (static predistortion with entropy loading). Under rapid thermal steps, TRACEL achieves 6.863 Gbit/s, an 8.19 % gain over static joint loading, while updating only 6.48 % of blocks and remaining within 1.46 % of an oracle. All results come from a behavioral-model simulation and are not hardware measurements.</jats:p>
title: Thermally robust self-calibration and entropy loading for micro-LED links: a simulation study

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Lead‐free inorganic halide perovskites are attracting increasing interest as multifunctional materials for energy and optoelectronic applications. Here, we systematically investigate the structural, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and photocatalytic properties of cubic SrAgZ
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    (Z = Cl, Br, I) using first‐principles calculations. Structural properties were evaluated using GGA‐PBE, while the TB‐mBJ approach was employed for improved band‐gap prediction. The calculated band gaps are 2.91, 2.17, and 0.97 eV for SrAgCl
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    , SrAgBr
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    , and SrAgI
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    , respectively, indicating tunable electronic properties with halide substitution. Strong optical absorption, exceeding 10
                    <jats:sup>5</jats:sup>
                     cm
                    <jats:sup>−</jats:sup>
                    <jats:sup>1</jats:sup>
                    , and low UV reflectivity suggest favorable light‐interaction characteristics. BoltzTraP calculations within the constant relaxation‐time approximation reveal promising thermoelectric performance, with a maximum ZT of 0.71 for SrAgCl
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    at 1200 K. Band‐edge analysis indicates that direct overall water splitting is not feasible because the CBM positions are insufficiently negative for H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    evolution. Thus, the photocatalytic potential is discussed in terms of selected redox processes rather than overall hydrogen production. Overall, the calculated multifunctional properties suggest that SrAgZ
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    compounds warrant further investigation for optoelectronic, energy‐conversion, and selected photocatalytic applications.
                  </jats:p>
title:
Multifunctional Properties of SrAgZ
                    <sub>3</sub>
                    (Z = Cl, Br, I): A First‐Principles Investigation

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In upstream coherent passive optical networks (PONs), the challenge of coping with short bursts arises due to variations in received powers, carrier offsets, phase states, and digital signal processing residuals. While point-estimate adaptation may not provide calibrated reliability, fixed margins have the drawback of imposing constraints on power and spectral efficiency. To address this problem, the paper presents an approach called adaptive conformal finite block length (AC-FBLA), which consists of an optical line terminal controller that transforms recent signed residual estimates into the context-dependent and recency-weighted one-sided lower bound for burst SNR. Adaptive miscoverage feedback helps handle the issues of undercover, while the scheme uses a finite block length feasibility sieve for selecting the levels of launch power, modulation formats, and coding rates for each grant effectively. Using Monte Carlo simulations with 32 ONUs, 25 GBd transmissions, 1,024 symbol payload cases, six coded modes, four powers of launch, and four regimes of channel estimation enabled the teams to reach a high 97.67–97.77 % coverage compared to the target of 98 %. Therefore, one can see that the offered solution can improve the block error rate by 87.3–97.8 % compared to point estimate adaptation and reach improvements in spectral efficiency of 45.3–79.6 %.</jats:p>
title: Adaptive conformal finite-blocklength link adaptation for burst-mode coherent passive optical networks

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Alzheimer's disease (AD) continues to be the leading cause of dementia
worldwide, due to its complicated, multifactorial pathophysiology. To shift the AD paradigm from
reactive to proactive, from a specific time to a precision medicine intervention strategy, this study
examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) as a potential linking point for multi-omics data, new
fluid biomarkers, and developing medicines.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A thorough search was conducted in clinical trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov) and peerreviewed
literature (PubMed, Scopus). Without going too far into detail, this study discussed novel
anti-amyloid/anti-tau monoclonal antibody treatments, blood biomarkers (p-tau217, p-tau181), and
machine learning approaches for early diagnostic classification and for prediction modelling.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Recent breakthroughs in understanding that different disease-modifying treatments, such as
lecanemab and donanemab, can stop cognitive decline by targeting specific types of disease-causing
aggregates have greatly shortened diagnostic time through blood-based diagnostic markers. Importantly,
AI systems (e.g., structural MRI and multi-omics-based panels analyzed using Deep
Learning architectures) can predict conversion from Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) to overt AD
more than a year before the onset of clinical symptoms, with accuracy exceeding 90%. Sensitivity of
real-world trials is significantly enhanced by the use of Digital Biomarkers and remote cognitive
monitoring.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As a tool, AI is not discrete but serves as a coherent framework that can progressively
connect data from different biological systems (e.g., upstream molecular events such as amyloid
cascades, tauopathy, neuroinflammation) with downstream clinical events (phenotypes). The lack of
standardized datasets across different ethnic groups, algorithm interpretability (the "black box" problem),
and possible regulatory validation, however, is now preventing the full clinical translation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>With insulin injections, or even just the excitement of a new drug, the world of AD
research is transformed. The multimodal AI frameworks provide clinicians with ways to treat patients
with highly personalized, multi-targeted treatment strategies to capture AD pathology at its
asymptomatic early stage, by simultaneously computing genetic risk, neuroimaging features, and
plasma biomarker levels.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: AI-integrated Approaches in Alzheimer’s Disease: Linking Molecular Pathways, Biomarkers, and Emerging Therapies
